annotation_comments.text: Genetic variation involving NHSL3 may be a cause of atypical endothelial corneal dystrophy (ECD). The disease follows an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance in the identified patients. Clinical characteristics of patients with the atypical form of ECD include peripheral endothelial opacities, an opaque ring along limbus, central endothelial opacities, central stromal opacities and corneal edema. The early phenotype of this atypical ECD is characterized by multiple small white translucent spots located in the Descemet membrane of the peripheral cornea.
